RFC 7311 Section 3.4.3: "Then, when R1 changes the next hop of a route from R2 to R1, the AIGP TLV value MUST be increased by a non-zero amount." The preceding sentence describes a direct EBGP link on which no IGP is running. Q1: TestRFC7311DirectLinkCostNeverWrapsOrDisappears requires configured cost 7 to turn received 100 into final-wire 107 and verifies an exact route withdrawal for absent cost. TestAIGPForwardedMetricsReachFinalWire separately covers policy-link increment 7 with no IGP resolution and zero-cost refusal. TestRFC7311SourceLinkCostReachesRecipient enters general and RS cached forwarding with source costs 7 and 19, a deliberately different destination cost 43, no resolving IGP route, exact output metrics 107 and 119, unchanged-next-hop 100 controls and maximum boundaries. TestRFC7311UnknownCostWithdrawsUntilMetricRecovers checks both rails, unknown/zero costs and three advertisement histories; known distance 11 restores the original route as exactly 111 without another source UPDATE. Q2: using the destination cost, omitting or doubling the increment, dropping AIGP, or losing recovery fails exact wire values, prefix fields or frame counts. The panic/revert records prove producer dependence, not a semantic wrong-value mutation. After this source audit, main renewed all sixteen changed-unit/polarity bindings in job-refusal-rfc7311-renew-20feecf3.log, including both changed units' pairs for this requirement. The inspected log shows a clean baseline PASS followed by the expected producer-disabled panic FAIL for each distinct recorded tuple. Q3: valid source TLVs, explicit accepting policies/send grants, no interior route, different source/destination costs and immutable source bytes isolate link-cost provenance. Never-advertised routes correctly emit no withdrawal; already-advertised routes must emit an exact pure withdrawal. Withholding is Ze's chosen refusal when it cannot meet the nonzero increment, not an RFC mandate to withdraw.
